scope: Game-design questions and user answers only. Original options preserved when available. Dates in file names are America/Los_Angeles; provenance timestamps are UTC.
completeness: Recovered entries only; missing answers are explicitly marked. This is not a complete export of every chat or every historical interview.

entries.question:
❓ Q1 — What should the name make you feel first?

A. Pressure and survival: tense, dangerous, grounded.
B. A strange sci-fi world: mysterious and memorable.
C. Competition and combat: forceful and confrontational.

➡️ I recommend A, with a little of B.
options: A — Pressure and survival, with some mystery (recommended)
entries.answer_format: numbered-answer; spelling and option letters preserved
entries.interpretation: Historical answer; current rules and later corrections are in ../../current.json.

entries.question:
❓ Q2 — What kind of name appeals to you most?

A. A short invented word that could belong to our world.
B. A concrete place, event, or system inside the game.
C. A brief phrase with an interesting double meaning.

➡️ I recommend B: something that sounds like it belongs to the setting and can cover both future modes.
options: C — Phrase with a double meaning

entries.question:
❓ Q3 — Which logo direction should guide the next pass?

A. Mostly typography: clean, distinctive letters and one restrained detail.
B. Rough utilitarian lettering: markings you might find on arena equipment.
C. A small abstract symbol alongside simple lettering.

➡️ I recommend A. We can establish the name first, then give it a recognizable letterform.
entries.answer: A blend of b and c actually. I don’t like the direction you naturally went

entries.question:
❓ Q4 — What should the name refer to inside the game’s world?

A. The event or trial that squads enter.
B. The arena complex or territory they fight through.
C. The system or organization running the arenas.

➡️ I recommend A; it fits survival and competition without depending on one map.
entries.answer: A, maybe c would be a better direction. Naming the games?

❓ Q7 — Which equipment-marking style is closer to your taste?

A. A stamped identification mark: sturdy lettering, a few deliberate cuts, a compact abstract symbol.
B. Arena wayfinding: clean signs, route marks, and directional shapes.
C. A rough hand-applied mark used by the fighters themselves.

➡️ I recommend A, with restraint in the wear and texture.
entries.answer: A and some c, give me both and let me pick

entries.question:
❓ Q9 — Which of these feels closest to a game you’d want to name?

A. INTERLOCK — a possible name for the system controlling the arenas, gates, and progression.
B. CUTLINE — a possible name for the trial’s survival cutoff and the system enforcing it.
C. KORDEN — an invented name for the organization running the arenas; its meaning would come from the world.
D. CORDON — a name drawn from the enclosed territory and its controlling authority.

➡️ I recommend exploring INTERLOCK and KORDEN first. These are naming directions, not fixed lore or checked availability. You can reject the whole set and tell me what feels wrong.
entries.answer: I don’t like any of them, I like the concept of cutline and interlock the most but I don’t love it.
entries.answer_format: numbered-answer; spelling and option letters preserved

entries.question:
❓ Q10 — Is the second mode still the previously planned single-arena survival mode?

The saved plan has a roughly 20-minute run in one arena, compared with the current 45–60-minute route through multiple arenas. Newer lobby notes left its rules open, so I want to resolve that conflict before naming it.

➡️ I recommend keeping the single-arena survival concept; we can tune its duration later.
entries.interpretation: Historical answer; current rules and later corrections are in ../../current.json.

entries.question:
❓ Q11 — Which new game-title direction feels closest?

A. DEADBAND — a cold, unfamiliar program designation.
B. CROSSLOAD — an industrial name suggesting pressure carried by the squad.
C. LOADLINE — an operating limit, with the linked-arena idea underneath it.
D. REDUCT — a short invented designation for the controlling system or organization.

➡️ My pick to explore is DEADBAND. These are sound-and-feel proposals; none fixes the lore or has been checked for name conflicts yet. Reject all four if they still miss.
entries.answer: I like reduct, deadband is cool idea but not great sounding

entries.question:
❓ Q12 — Which pair of mode names feels best? The first name is the multi-arena run; the second is single-arena survival.

A. ADVANCE / HOLDOUT — clear and forceful.
B. TRAVERSE / CONTAINMENT — more industrial and in-world.
C. THE RUN / THE STAND — names fighters might use themselves.

➡️ I recommend A for menu clarity, but C may better match the rougher fighter-mark branding you asked to compare.

➡️ I recommend PROGRESSION RUN: the squad moves through arenas and develops its weapons during the run. We can keep your original wording if you prefer its sound.

➡️ I recommend finding a nearby variation that keeps the short, industrial sound you liked. The two logo styles can stay the same.

entries.question:
❓ Q15 — Which name should I use for the stamped and fighter-mark logo comparisons?

➡️ I recommend REDUKT. REDUCTA is slightly more distinct in sound. Both have existing uses outside games, so this is a concept choice rather than final availability clearance.

entries.question:
❓ Q16 — Which fresh direction has the most potential?

A. UNSPARED — a trial that gives the squad no easy way through.
B. EXACTOR — a cold name for the authority running the arenas.
C. NULLMARK — an unfamiliar designation from the arena system.
D. HARD LIMIT — a pressure threshold the squad has to survive.

➡️ My strongest pick is UNSPARED for the stakes, with EXACTOR closest to the controlling-organization idea. No exact game-title match surfaced for these in the limited check; this is still a shortlist.
entries.answer: Is this the game name or mode name?
